_about: Register and word-choice rules for spoken Dhivehi addressed to an audience: ads, presenters, video voice-over. Checked by dhivehi_rules/dba_rules.py only when a context is given (check(text, context='ad'), or --context on the command line). Without a context nothing here runs, so the spelling and word-division checks behave exactly as before. Read guides/spoken_register.md for the evidence and reasoning behind each rule. Patterns are Python regexes; [ހ-޿] is the Thaana block. severity 'error' = do not ship; 'warn' = reported with a leading ~, judge in context. 'replace' is an re.Match.expand() template that gives the suggested form, keeping any case ending.

contexts.ad: advertisement or promotional copy, spoken or on screen
contexts.presenter: a presenter, host or reviewer speaking to camera
contexts.video: any narration or voice-over addressed to viewers

rules.why: Scripture-translation register (Quran and hadith 'O you people'), not how anyone addresses viewers. Public speakers say ތިޔަބޭފުޅުން or ހުރިހާ ބޭފުޅުން.
rules.evidence: Speeches: ތިޔަބޭފުޅުން 2,595 to ތިޔަބައިމީހުން 114. News (8 sites): 70% of ތިޔަބައިމީހުން (3,263 of 4,680) are in sentences that also quote or cite Quran/hadith. Promotional news items: 26, against 128 for ތިޔަ(ބޭފުޅުން).

rules.why: ކަލޭ / ކަލޭމެން is intimate or rude second person (quarrels, friends, fiction dialogue). Never to an audience. ކަލޭގެފާނު, the honorific for prophets, is not matched.
rules.evidence: Speeches: ކަލޭ + ކަލޭމެން 23 in 469 speeches, against ތިޔަބޭފުޅުން 2,595. In news it shows up in quoted dialogue and fiction.

rules.why: ތިބާ is the written generic 'you/one' of essays, proverbs and advice columns. It reads as a printed slogan, not a person talking. Fine on a poster; in speech prefer ތިޔަބޭފުޅުން.
rules.evidence: Speeches: ތިބާ 4. News: 5,931; sampled hits are opinion and advice columns, a recurring religious column, and slogans.

rules.why: އަހަރެން is the private, written-narrative 'I' (fiction, diaries, translated foreign quotes). A speaker in public says އަޅުގަނޑު.
rules.evidence: Speeches: އަޅުގަނޑު 16,614 to އަހަރެން 13. Majlis sittings: 586,790 to 148. In news, އަހަރެން appears in short stories and in translations of foreign people's quotes; Maldivian officials are quoted with އަޅުގަނޑު.

rules.why: Plural of the same informal 'I'. A business speaking to customers says އަޅުގަނޑުމެން.
rules.evidence: Speeches: އަޅުގަނޑުމެން 20,315 to އަހަރެމެން 24. Promotional news items: 'އަޅުގަނޑުމެންގެ ކަސްޓަމަރުން' 279 times.

rules.why: ތިމަންނަ is the 'I' of official letters, legal statements and oaths. Too stiff for a presenter.
rules.evidence: Majlis records 8,782 (formal statements); speeches 171; promotional news items 177.

rules.why: Plain imperatives are how you talk to a child or a close friend. Ads ask the audience with the honorific forms: ގުޅުއްވާ, ބައްލަވާ / ބައްލަވާލައްވާ, ގަންނަވާ, ވަޑައިގަންނަވާ, ހޯއްދަވާ, ...ކުރައްވާ.
rules.evidence: '<7-digit number> އަށް ގުޅުއްވާ/ގުޅުއްވުމުން' 1,396 to '... ގުޅާ' 275 in news (the plain ones are mostly reported instructions, not ad copy).

rules.why: English word order ('delivery free'). Dhivehi puts the modifier first: ހިލޭ ޑެލިވަރީ.
rules.evidence: News: ހިލޭ ޑެލިވަރީ 399, ފްރީ ޑެލިވަރީ 114 (mostly a film title), ޑެލިވަރީ ހިލޭ / ޑެލިވަރީ ފްރީ 0.

rules.why: 'WhatsApp us' as a verb is English. Written Dhivehi copy says ވަޓްސްއެޕް މެދުވެރިކޮށް (via WhatsApp) with a real verb: މެސެޖުކުރައްވާ, އޯޑަރުކުރެއްވޭނެ. Casual speech does say 'ވަޓްސްއެޕް ކޮށްލައްވާ', hence warn, not error.
rules.evidence: News: ވަޓްސްއެޕް ކުރައްވާ 1, ވަޓްސްއެޕްކުރައްވާ 0; ވަޓްސްއެޕް މެދުވެރިކޮށް 253. Real copy (halinews): 'ވަޓްސްއަޕް (WhatsApp) މެދުވެރިކޮށް ވެސް މެސެޖުކުރައްވައިގެން އޯޑަރު ކުރެއްވޭނެއެވެ'.

rules.why: 'Have a good day / Good morning' translated word for word. Not used as a greeting or sign-off. Dhivehi wishes: ބާއްޖަވެރި ދުވަހަކަށް / ރޭގަނޑަކަށް އެދެން.
rules.evidence: News: ހެޔޮ ދުވަހެއް/ހެނދުނެއް/ރެއެއް 5, none of them a greeting; ބާއްޖަވެރި ދުވަހަކަށް/ރޭގަނޑަކަށް 120. A TV news sign-off quoted on esfiya: 'ޚަބަރު ބެއްލެވީތީ ޝުކުރިއްޔާ.. އެންމެ ބޭފުޅުންނަށް ވެސް ބާއްޖަވެރި، އަމާން، ރައްކާތެރި ރެޔަކަށް...'.

rules.why: 'Thank you for watching' in English order. Dhivehi gives the reason first: ބެއްލެވީތީ ޝުކުރިއްޔާ.
rules.evidence: News: 'ބެއްލެވީތީ ޝުކުރިއްޔާ' 3 (TV programme and news sign-offs), 'ޝުކުރިއްޔާ ބެއްލެވީތީ' 0.

rules.why: Coined in earlier generated scripts and not found in the corpus or Radheef: ފެންފައިޕު (0 hits) for 'faucet', މަލަ ނާރާ (the single hit is a mis-split of ހަމަލަ) for 'rust-proof'. Use the product name (ޕުލް އައުޓް ފޯސެޓް) or a neutral word (ބާވަތް), and say what the material is instead (ސްޓެއިންލެސް ސްޓީލުން ހަދާފައިވާ).
rules.evidence: corpus_vocab.tsv + 26 crawled news sites: ފެންފައިޕު 0, ފެނުގެ ޓޭޕު 0; ޓޭޕް in the corpus is adhesive or recording tape. ފޯސެޓް appears only in translated instruction data.
